stories.headline: Iran will not remain in state of "neither war nor peace": Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf
stories.title: Iran will not remain in state of "neither war nor peace": Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf
stories.summary: Tehran , November 15 : Denouncing Washington's policies towards Tehran, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf has underscored that the Islamic Republic refuses to remain trapped in a condition of "neither war nor peace", according to Mehr, a semi-official Iranian news agency. Addressing lawmakers during an open session of parliament on Sunday, the legislative chief asserted, “We do not care whether the US chooses the path of negotiations or war. If it accepts our seven reasonable conditions, the door to an agreement will be open.” Warning the US against committing further miscalculations, Qalibaf cautioned that the nation's formidable armed forces would dictate the territorial parameters of any ensuing conflict. On a national commemorative occasion dedicated to the aerospace sector and marking the death anniversary of Major General Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, widely recognised as the architect of the country's missile development, the speaker also paid tribute to industry commanders. Highlighting the strategic milestones achieved by the IRGC Aerospace Force, Qalibaf noted how the division had leveraged its foundational principles to turn obstacles into advantages, as reported by Mehr. He stated that the force had successfully countered strategies pursued by foreign adversaries while inspiring populations across the region and supporting Palestinian youth. Emphasising its achievements, he said, “Today, the Aerospace Force of the country, relying upon the divine principles and Quranic tenet, has turned 'impossible' into 'possible', threats into opportunities and also frustrated all the malicious plots orchestrated by the criminal Zionist regime and the terrorist US government against Iran, bestowing hope and dignity to the resilient people of Iran, freedom-seeking nations of the region and the world, particularly, the oppressed children of Palestine.” Turning his attention to remarks delivered by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Qalibaf dismissed them as reflecting diplomatic frustration. “The absurd statements and immoral language of the US Treasury Secretary reveal their profound desperation in the face of the Islamic Republic’s authority on the international stage. Someone who has fled their own home for military bunkers out of fear of looming threats would do better to reflect on their strategic failures in the Persian Gulf, rather than insulting great and heroic nations,” he said. The top parliamentarian reiterated that such provocative rhetoric merely exposed profound uneasiness regarding the expanding international influence of the Iranian state, with Mehr highlighting the condemnation. Meanwhile, tensions between Iran and the United States have also extended to military installations in the Gulf region. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its forces carried out a drone attack targeting a US radar system at a military base in Bahrain, according to an official release broadcast by Iranian state media. Elaborating on the military operation in a statement published via Telegram by the state broadcaster, the IRGC said, “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force.” Earlier, Bahrain's Interior Ministry had released two separate advisory alerts on the social media platform X, warning of potential security hazards. This marked the Gulf nation's first warnings of this nature since September. Adding to concerns over Iran's military capabilities, a report by The Wall Street Journal, citing US intelligence officials, said Tehran could still possess up to 2,500 missiles in its arsenal. The assessment follows claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that it had recently struck the radar of a US air defence site at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain in retaliation for US military actions. Despite months of sustained US and Israeli strikes aimed at crippling its weapons infrastructure, intelligence officials estimate that Iran retains between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, according to the Journal's report. Alongside these developments, tensions have also escalated around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines in and around the waterway, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy and Armed Forces' Navy said on Saturday (local time), as Iranian forces warned vessels against entering restricted maritime areas. According to Iranian state media outlet Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), the IRGC Navy said in a recent statement that two oil tankers attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz without authorisation had exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines. Explaining the circumstances of the incidents, the IRGC Navy said the vessels had been attempting to navigate the strategically important waterway secretly, with their navigation and automatic identification systems switched off. "An hour ago, two offending oil tankers, which were secretly attempting to transit the unauthorised Strait of Hormuz with their navigation and automatic identification systems turned off, exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines," the statement said, as reported by IRIB. The Iranian naval force further claimed that two other tankers attempting to pass through the strait had turned back after receiving warnings from the IRGC's Naval Traffic Control Centre. "After the explosion of these two tankers, two other tankers that were attempting to secretly pass through the Strait of Hormuz heeded warnings from the IRGC's Naval Traffic Control Centre and returned to the waters of the Persian Gulf," the statement added. In a separate statement, the Armed Forces Navy also reported an incident involving another oil tanker east of the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that the vessel had caught fire after striking a naval mine. According to its Public Relations department, the tanker had been operating in what it described as an unsafe and prohibited area despite earlier warnings. It had also switched off its tracking and identification systems. "This morning, an oil tanker that had been operating in the unsafe and prohibited area east of the Strait of Hormuz, ignoring previous warnings and turning off its tracking and identification systems, caught fire and stopped after hitting a naval mine," the statement said. Following the incident, the Armed Forces' Navy warned other shipping operators that vessels entering the restricted maritime zone would face similar consequences. "Without a doubt, any offending tanker that travels in the restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz will be set on fire by hitting naval mines," it said. The statement also criticised tanker owners for sending vessels into the restricted area, accusing them of relying on assurances from US President Donald Trump. "It is unfortunate that tanker owners, without learning from the fate of other offending vessels, trusting the nonsense of the criminal US president, are sending their capital into the mine war and throwing it into the fire," the statement added. These developments come amid escalating tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel, with the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a key flashpoint in the ongoing West Asia conflict. (ANI)

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan to move towards Andhra coast by November 19, rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu, Bengal
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to move towards Andhra coast by November 19, rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu, Bengal
stories.summary: The cyclone is expected to bring rains to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said.
The department announced that the cycline is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19.

The Regional Meteorological Centre issued a Nowcast alert at 1 p.m. in Tamilnadu, valid till 4 p.m. for light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over Cuddalore, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Nagappattinam, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Thiruvarur and Viluppuram districts and Karaikal and Puducherry.

According to the latest weather report, Saturday's (November 14) well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5:30 a.m. today.

It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17.

The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the State from Monday (November 16).
According to the bulletin, during the last 24 hours ending at 8:30 a.m. on Sunday (November 15), rainfall occurred in several districts, including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram and Kanyakumari.
The IMD alerted that the cyclone will bring heavy rain to some districts of West Bengal from November 19 to 21.
It will bring heavy rain to the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, the department said.
A downpour is also likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.

stories.headline: Third cyclone in three weeks? IMD warns of severe storm by Nov 17, Odisha on high alert
stories.title: Third cyclone in three weeks? IMD warns of severe storm by Nov 17, Odisha on high alert
stories.summary: Odisha has placed all districts, particularly its southern and coastal regions, on alert as the state prepares for a possible third cyclone in three weeks
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In its latest update, the IMD said the depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwards at a speed of 10 kmph during the three hours preceding 8.30 am on November 15.
The system was centred about 840 km east-southeast of Chennai, 1,010 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 1,130 km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha.

"It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of the south & adjoining West-central Bay of Bengal on 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal on 17th November, 2026," the IMD said.
The weather office added that the system could intensify further and move northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following two days.
However, its exact landfall location has not yet been confirmed.
Odisha Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the state was taking precautionary measures following the impact of Cyclone Arnab in October and Cyclone Murasu earlier this month.
"Though the IMD has not forecast the landfall of the impending cyclone so far, we have put districts on alert keeping in view of the experience," Pujari said.
Cyclone Arnab made landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh on October 28, triggering devastating floods in several southern Odisha districts.
Cyclone Murasu subsequently brought rainfall to the region.
Authorities have been directed to remain prepared for possible heavy rainfall, flooding and evacuation requirements.
A 24-hour control room will remain operational in every district.
Personnel from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), Fire Services and emergency teams have been placed on standby.

article_sentences: A cyclonic storm forming over the south Bay of Bengal will bring heavy rain to some districts of West Bengal from November 19 to 21, the India Meteorological Department said on Sunday.
The weather system, which lay over the southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal as a depression on Sunday morning, is very likely to move north-northwestward.
It is likely to gradually intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over east-central Bay of Bengal on November 17, according to the weather department.
It will bring heavy rain to the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, it said.
A downpour is also likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 km per hour in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.
A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, it said.
Darjeeling was the coldest place in West Bengal on Sunday with a minimum temperature of 8.2 degrees Celsius, while Kolkata recorded a low of 21.3 degrees Celsius.

stories.headline: NITI Aayog to launch five national workshops to draw lessons from PM Modi’s 25 years as head of government
stories.title: NITI Aayog to launch five national workshops to draw lessons from PM Modi’s 25 years as head of government
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 15: NITI Aayog will launch a series of five National Workshops on 17 November 2026 to draw lessons from twenty-five years of the Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, as Head of Government. The series will study this quarter century of public leadership so that its lessons become part of the nation’s shared knowledge. It will document the experiences of those who were part of this journey and translate them into knowledge that benefits all. The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat on 7 October 2001. After serving for more than twelve years in that office, he assumed office as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and is now serving his third successive term. With the completion of twenty-five years on 7 October 2026, this marks the longest continuous tenure at the head of an elected government in India. Throughout this period, governance has been anchored in the idea of the Pradhan Sevak, under which every office of government exists to serve the citizens. Antyodaya has set the measure of progress at the last person. Jan Bhagidari has made development a people’s movement. The principle of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas has further strengthened this as a shared national undertaking. The goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047 has provided this approach a long horizon, asking every institution to plan and act for India as it approaches the centenary of Independence. Much of what India has learnt about governing at this scale is held in the experience of the officers, institutions and citizens who took and carried through these decisions. The series will record their first-hand accounts and examine them with academic rigour. It will develop them into institutional learning material, including case studies, research papers and teaching material, for civil servants, training institutions, universities, students and the wider public. The five National Workshops will be focus on the following governance themes: “Leadership as Mission” in November 2026, “Governance as Delivery” in January 2027, “Development as Inclusion” in April 2027, “Civilisational Identity” in July 2027 and “India as a Global Force” in September 2027. The first National Workshop, “Leadership as Mission”, will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 17th November 2026. It will study leadership through the specific decisions in which it becomes visible and the manner in which those decisions are translated into outcomes for citizens. Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog, will welcome the participants and Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, will deliver the opening remarks. Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, will deliver the inaugural keynote address, and Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank, will deliver a keynote address. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, will set out the framework of the workshop. Four first-hand accounts from those who were directly part of significant decisions will form the core of the day. Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Gujarat, will speak on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake. Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC, will speak on the response to Covid-19. Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, will speak on Lakhpati Didi. Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO, will share his experience on the opening up of the space economy. A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog. The panellists will include Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi. Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will close the workshop and launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. Through the Sankalpa, civil servants across the country will commit to a specific change in their own leadership practice. Around 900 participants are expected to attend the workshop, of whom 250 will participate directly in the deliberations. These will include 150 government officers, including Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments and District Collectors of Aspirational Districts. The participants will also include 25 students of leading institutions and universities, and 50 community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The group discussions will be guided by 25 case facilitators trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission. The proceedings will be streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform.

The five National Workshops will be focus on the following governance themes: “Leadership as Mission” in November 2026, “Governance as Delivery” in January 2027, “Development as Inclusion” in April 2027, “Civilisational Identity” in July 2027 and “India as a Global Force” in September 2027.
The first National Workshop, “Leadership as Mission”, will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 17th November 2026.
It will study leadership through the specific decisions in which it becomes visible and the manner in which those decisions are translated into outcomes for citizens.
Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog, will welcome the participants and Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, will deliver the opening remarks.
Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, will deliver the inaugural keynote address, and Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank, will deliver a keynote address.
Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, will set out the framework of the workshop.
Four first-hand accounts from those who were directly part of significant decisions will form the core of the day.
Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Gujarat, will speak on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake.
Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC, will speak on the response to Covid-19.
Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, will speak on Lakhpati Didi.
Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO, will share his experience on the opening up of the space economy.
A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog.

The panellists will include Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi.
Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will close the workshop and launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform.
Through the Sankalpa, civil servants across the country will commit to a specific change in their own leadership practice.
These will include 150 government officers, including Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments and District Collectors of Aspirational Districts.
The participants will also include 25 students of leading institutions and universities, and 50 community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes.
The group discussions will be guided by 25 case facilitators trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission.
The proceedings will be streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform.

article_sentences: New Delhi: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that voters whose names are missing from draft electoral rolls despite having been enrolled earlier can apply afresh through Form 6 without fear of prosecution.
In an affidavit filed before the court, the poll panel said Chief Electoral.
Officers (CEOs) had been asked to give wide publicity to the clarification, including in local languages.

“It had been brought to the notice of the Commission that some apprehensions were expressed that applicants who were enrolled as voters in previous electoral roll(s) but whose names did not appear in the draft Electoral Roll during the SIR — by filing Form 6, may face action for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, on account of the fact that they were enrolled as voters in the previous electoral roll(s).

“In order to allay such misapprehensions, the Commission… has clarified that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their name did not appear in the draft electoral roll during the SIR, provided that applicant/elector is not already enrolled in any other Parliamentary or Assembly Constituency and the declaration made is otherwise in accordance with law,” the affidavit said.

The poll panel submitted that it had also taken note of the Supreme Court’s suggestion to reach out to left-out ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate) voters to facilitate their inclusion in the electoral roll.
“The Commission decided to take certain further measures in the interest of the voters.
The Commission has inter alia issued directions by its communication dated November 6, 2026, to the Chief Electoral Officers of the states/UTs where the SIR is ongoing,” it said.
The EC said it had asked the CEOs to allow voters to submit duly filled Enumeration Forms (Annexure.
A) to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Booth Level Officer (BLO) for their current ordinary residence.
“Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed Enumeration Form (Annexure A) with the Annexure-B statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the Enumeration Form.
They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members.

stories.headline: India should become developer, innovator and global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath
stories.title: India should become developer, innovator and global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 15: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday called for making India not merely a user of advanced technologies, but also a developer, innovator and global leader in critical domains, as he emphasised the need to strengthen the country’s non-destructive testing ecosystem for better preparedness and self-reliance. He virtually addressed the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation & Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace. Singh stressed the importance of developing indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, promoting consistent quality assurance practices and ensuring the accuracy, reliability and integrity of testing results, particularly in strategic applications. He asserted that there can be no compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications. "We must strengthen our indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software," the minister asserted. "Developing domestic capabilities in these areas is essential for reducing technological dependencies and securing critical defence supply chains. We must promote consistent quality assurance practices across the entire defence industrial ecosystem," he said. Public sector undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups and MSMEs have an "important role to play" in this endeavour. "We must ensure that inspection results are accurate, reliable and traceable, and are based on robust procedures and appropriate standards followed by assessment by qualified professionals,” the defence minister said. The three-day conference, organised by the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing in Hyderabad, Telangana, has brought together over 2,000 professionals, researchers, industry experts and students to deliberate on the latest advancements, emerging technologies and applications in non-destructive testing (NDT), the defence ministry said. Singh stressed that the NDT technologies enable examination of the integrity of materials, components and structures without causing any damage to them. Elucidating the concept, he said that just as ultrasound and X-rays help examine the human body without surgical intervention, NDT techniques enable the detection of internal defects in critical components without dismantling or damaging them. Singh underlined that as Indian defence systems become increasingly sophisticated, every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process must meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. “Hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce the service life of equipment and, in critical situations, jeopardise mission success. We need to move beyond a culture of merely identifying defects towards actively preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of the manufacturing process,” he said. Singh stressed that the progress of a nation depends not merely on the technologies it develops, but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems it builds. In defence applications, including missiles, aircraft, naval platforms and spacecraft, quality is not merely a manufacturing requirement but an essential element of operational reliability and national security, he said. Emphasising the strategic significance of the sector, Singh said that for a country aspiring to achieve technological leadership, the importance of NDT cannot be overstated. He asserted that India's pursuit of “Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance)” in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity. Underscoring the importance of keeping pace with the rapidly changing global security environment, Singh said indigenous weapons, platforms and supporting systems "must deliver the highest levels of reliability and performance at all times". He urged professionals associated with the NDT sector to continuously upgrade their capabilities and keep the spirit of innovation alive in sync with emerging technologies and evolving security requirements. On the technological transformation underway in the field of non-destructive evaluation, he stressed that artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, advanced sensors, digital twins and predictive analytics are significantly expanding the possibilities of inspection and structural health monitoring. These technologies, he said, can improve the speed and consistency of inspections, facilitate the analysis of complex data and identify patterns that may not be easily detectable through conventional methods. Singh emphasised that the future lies in the intelligent integration of established inspection techniques with advanced digital technologies to make inspection processes more accurate, efficient and responsive to emerging industrial requirements. The minister called upon India to move beyond merely adopting these technologies and develop indigenous solutions tailored to its strategic and industrial requirements. Investment in research, advanced equipment, software and skilled manpower would strengthen domestic capabilities and enable Indian technologies to find markets internationally, he said.

stories.headline: ONGC takes charge of Cambay block as Vedanta records ₹379 crore impairment
stories.title: ONGC takes charge of Cambay block as Vedanta records ₹379 crore impairment
stories.summary: Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'takes charge' in title weight 40
article_sentences: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.

The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025.
The contract for the Cambay block expired on June 29, 2023.
Vedanta and its joint venture partners had applied for an extension on June 28, 2021, under the government's 2017 extension policy.
Vedanta's writ petition was dismissed on July 22, 2026, resulting in the vacation of an interim stay that had earlier directed that status quo be maintained.
ONGC subsequently took over the block and applied for a petroleum lease on July 28, 2026.
The legal dispute, however, remains unresolved.
Vedanta appealed against the single-judge order before a division bench of the Delhi High Court.
